thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated p95 latency and request queueing observed for inference gateway in us-west-2 starting at 2026-03-15T09:07:48Z. Metric: p95 token latency spike from ~120ms -> 2.1s. Error rates stable. Auto-scaling hasn't caught up.

maria: seeing the same on dashboards, prefix cache hit rate dropped ~30% which explains extra KV reads. looks like sudden traffic shape change to long-context chat sessions.

ryan: paging into rotation. I'm oncall. starting a quick blast radius mitigation: will route new sessions to us-east-1 and spin up extra dedicated workers in us-west. assigning tasks below.

sam: +1. can you draft a short status page blurb? Handoff to me if you need posting.

paul: investigating kernel/queue stats now. initial hypothesis: batching windows increased due to sticky long contexts; that caused token emission stalls. I can force smaller batching window on the runtime to cut latency at cost of higher GPU utilization.

maria: ok plan: 1) enable region fallback for new requests (route primary->us-east-1) 2) reduce batching window to 20ms on us-west runtime 3) enable quantized model variant as fallback for non-critical tiers. doing 1 and 2 now.

ryan: I'll take 1 and 2. paul, can you prepare commands for 2 and 3?

paul: command snippets:
```
# shrink batching window
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/runtime/us-west-2/config -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' -d '{"batching_ms":20}'

# enable model fallback (quantized)
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/routing -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' -d '{"policy":"region-fallback","fallback_model":"gptq-medium"}'
```

maria: applied batching change on us-west runtime. observing p95 drop starting. moving to enable routing policy now.

sam: status page draft below — please edit: 
"We are currently experiencing elevated latency in our us-west region affecting some inference requests. Engineers have applied reduced batching windows and enabled regional fallbacks to us-east. Traffic is routing to healthy capacity while we continue to scale workers. We expect user-facing latency to improve within 30-45 minutes. No data loss or model correctness impact identified."

emily: good. CS ready to send customer notice. I'll tailor for customers on reserved capacity vs hosted. we should include recommended workaround: pin to us-east region or temporarily reduce max_context to 2048 for long chat sessions.

karen: ops/legal note: any customer-facing line on root cause should be conservative. avoid saying "bug" — say "traffic pattern change" or "unexpected load shape."

ryan: assigned owners: routing & status page = sam, runtime batching = maria/paul, dedicated pool scale = me. ETA initial mitigation 15m, expect p95 ~normal in 30-45m. leaving this thread now but i'll keep monitoring and update every 10m. @sam pls escalate if no improvement.

sam: posted status page update: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/3525 (draft link) — copied above blurb, added ETA 45m.

incident-bot: Incident assigned to ryan. Severity: S2. Pager escalations set for 10m.

paul: quantized fallback enabled for non-enterprise tiers. monitoring perf. early signal: latency for routed traffic to us-east ~110ms p95. Good.

maria: us-west p95 down from 2.1s -> 360ms after batching change, further improving as autoscaler provisions more workers. cache warm-up in progress.

emily: CS template (short):
"Hi <Customer>,
We are investigating elevated latency impacting inference requests in the us-west region. Our engineers have applied mitigations: routing traffic to alternate region, adjusting runtime batching, and enabling a performance fallback model. You may see improved latency within the next 30-45 minutes. If you need immediate relief, we can pin your traffic to us-east or enable fallback now — reply and we'll action it. Apologies for the disruption.
— Redwood Support"

karen: approved the customer template with minor wording tweak.

ryan: next steps: continue to monitor metrics + tracing, confirm autoscaler finishes spin-up, verify no regression in output quality for fallback model. if quality alerts trigger, we'll rollback fallback and throttle ingress.

sam: agreed. if things stabilize, we'll close incident and post summary with timeline and RCA.

paul: flagging one follow-up: need a post-incident task to tune prefix cache heuristics so long-context bursts don't evict useful entries.

maria: noted. adding ticket in eng-runtime backlog.

ryan: thanks team. I'll post next update at +10m or sooner if things change. :thumbsup:
